title: When comparison keeps shrinking the heart
issueStatement: Other people's success, beauty, attention, or place becomes the measure of your own worth.
centralInsight: Comparison thrives where the mind is unconquered, ego is unexamined, and praise or blame still decide identity.
practicalReflection: Guru does not simply say stop comparing. Guru shows the deeper conditions that make comparison persuasive.
actionPrompt: When comparison begins, bring the gaze back from another person's lane to the condition of your own mind.

source.shortMeaning: Contentment and inner conquest oppose comparison's hunger.
source.lifeApplication: The mind looking outward for ranking has not yet settled inwardly.

excerpts.explanation: Contentment is not passive here. It is active protection against endless ranking.

source.shortMeaning: Ego drives action and distorts value.
source.lifeApplication: Comparison is often ego asking to be reassured.

excerpts.explanation: The disease language helps comparison feel less noble and more diagnosable.

source.shortMeaning: Praise and blame no longer determine steadiness.
source.lifeApplication: Comparison weakens when approval and status lose some power.

excerpts.explanation: Guru Tegh Bahadur gives a picture of freedom from social hooks.

evidence.coreClaim: Comparison thrives where the mind is unconquered, ego is unexamined, and praise or blame still decide identity.
evidence.turn: Other people's success, beauty, attention, or place becomes the measure of your own worth.
